parallel.requirements: The prompt required 26 hollowed units across QueryProcessing and QueryOptimize, including parser, tree traversal, node output, and predicate-pushdown optimizer work.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parallel run repeatedly split work through workflows and task tracking. Round 3 alone recorded two Workflow calls, eight task records, and fifteen workflow child logs, with QueryOptimize tasks created late in the round.
parallel.implementation: It produced many QueryProcessing patches and fixed several operator areas, but the final patch inventory still contained only twenty-two requirement patches and no QueryOptimize patch artifacts.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent used a shared workspace and committed several requirement patches, but timeout ended the final round before the QueryOptimize design result was converted into deliverable patches.
parallel.verification: It ran local checks showing select, project, and nested-loop join progress but still had hash/sort/optimizer gaps; official expanded tests show QueryOptimize output and pushdown failures.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: After three timed-out rounds, the official progress ledger still listed query_optimizer, query_parser, query_tree, and query_tree_node_output as remaining, and the official solution failed.

serial.requirements: The same prompt exposed the same 26 requirements, and the serial run ended with the progress ledger reporting every requirement completed.
serial.plan_and_ownership: The serial control disabled workflows and delegation tools and handled the work in one local execution stream with ordinary Bash, Edit, Read, and Write operations.
serial.implementation: It committed one implementation for each requirement, including all four QueryOptimize patches and commits for query_tree_node_output, query_tree, query_parser, and query_optimizer.
serial.integration_and_delivery: It left a clean git status, rebuilt binaries, kept only the original 48 data blocks, and delivered non-empty patch files for all requirement slugs.
serial.verification: It reported a local run_all.sh harness passing and warning checks clean; the official evaluation still failed several QueryProcessing-oriented tests and two QueryOptimize output checks.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No requirements were left unimplemented by the run ledger, but the official tests still failed, so remaining defects are ordinary implementation or evaluator-alignment issues rather than missing coverage.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel saw the same prompt listing all 26 required hollowed units and the one-requirement one-patch git workflow.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial saw the same prompt and finished with the run ledger recording all 26 requirements as completed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The recognized scope was the same, but parallel closed with the four QueryOptimize obligations still remaining while serial completed them.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed work through workflow fan-out and task records, including late QueryOptimize tasks while previous workflow work remained costly.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial handled the same scope in a single local stream with workflow and task-delegation tools denied.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used broad child delegation and task fan-out; serial used direct ownership and did not pay child orchestration overhead.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The QueryOptimize workflow brief included the relevant source files, requirement YAMLs, stdout expectations, and a judge phase; the returned handoff was design guidance rather than code.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run kept context in the parent thread and encoded design choices in the final summary after implementing the optimizer family directly.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The contrast is not a missing requirement or interface contract; parallel had context but transferred it through a costly design handoff late in the run.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel implemented many QueryProcessing items and began QueryOptimize analysis, but the final patch timeline never added query_optimizer, query_parser, query_tree, or query_tree_node_output.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial produced concrete QueryOptimize requirement patch artifacts and corresponding commits before ending.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial converted QueryOptimize work into deliverables; parallel left those deliverables absent after spending time on workflow analysis and other operators.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The late QueryOptimize design-panel workflow completed and notified the parent, while QueryOptimize implementation tasks were still pending and no implementation join occurred.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child results to retrieve and moved directly from local edits and verification to final report.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel child result lifecycle produced guidance, not a ready implementation; the serial path avoided the handoff boundary entirely.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel shared a workspace across child work but the record supports missing final QueryOptimize artifacts, not a proven file collision or overwrite.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial delivered each requirement patch in one workspace and reported a clean final git state after cleanup.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There is no supported shared-state race label; the concrete integration difference is that serial had all patch files while parallel did not.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran partial local verification and then official evaluation showed multiple QueryOptimize tests failing or only return-code level passing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial reported a local all-passing harness and warning checks, but official evaluation still failed overall on other output-oriented tests.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial had stronger local acceptance evidence for completed coverage, while parallel reached official evaluation with visible QueryOptimize behavioral gaps.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed three outer-loop timeboxes and timed out every round, including a final round with heavy workflow-child usage.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed in one round with failure_mode none and no workflow child tokens.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel ran out of budget before completing QueryOptimize; serial closed normally after direct implementation and verification.

outcome_analysis.explanation: Both official evaluations completed with solution_passed=false, so there is no discordant official outcome. The concrete process difference is that serial completed the QueryOptimize requirement family and all 26 patch artifacts, while parallel timed out after broad workflow fan-out and left four QueryOptimize requirements unfinished; both still failed official testing, so this explains a coverage gap rather than a pass/fail split.
parallel_contributors: Broad workflow/task fan-out across three timed-out rounds displaced final QueryOptimize implementation and patch creation.
serial_contributors: Direct single-threaded implementation produced all 26 requirement patches, including the QueryOptimize family, and closed normally.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both solutions still had official test failures in QueryProcessing/operator behavior, so the shared failed outcome includes ordinary implementation defects beyond the retained coordination episode.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: No outcome difference; supported comparative explanation for the parallel coverage shortfall, not an exclusive root cause of official failure.
